key_insight: The study shows that reinforcement learning can improve a language model’s clinical reasoning in oncology by using partially verifiable, patient-specific rewards from real-world decision processes.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help support more structured, sequential treatment planning for colon cancer when multiple reasonable choices exist under incomplete patient information.
method: Formulated colon cancer treatment planning as an interactive RL task under partial observability
Built process-aware rewards from real clinical records to guide information gathering and treatment selection
Optimized Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with GRPO and GDPO and evaluated reasoning alignment
evidence_signal: In the abstract, the GDPO-trained policy improved Mean@3 scalar clinical reward by 79.60% over the base Llama and surpassed GPT-5.2 by 18.82% in the same interactive environment.
watch_item: The environment is still a simulation of partially observed clinical decisions, so real-world deployment would need careful validation for safety, robustness, and clinician oversight.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning In Partially Verifiable Environments for Colon Cancer Treatment Planning
